Transparent conducting oxides

Transparent conducting oxide thin films

Transparent electrodes must transmit light while conducting electrical current. Achieving both properties depends on the interaction between deposition conditions, oxidation, and the resulting film structure. My MSc research at IIT Ropar investigated this relationship in antimony-doped tin oxide films.

Back to Research & Engineering Projects

IIT Ropar · Published work

I fabricated metallic precursor layers by vacuum thermal evaporation and converted them into Sb-doped SnO₂ through controlled post-oxidation. I varied precursor thickness and processing conditions to examine how the coupled deposition and oxidation steps influenced the final film.

I characterized crystal structure with XRD, measured optical transmission, and evaluated film thickness and electrical resistivity. Assessing these properties together allowed me to compare processing conditions in terms of both optical and electrical behavior.

The resulting first-author study on 5 wt% Sb-doped SnO₂, published in AIP Conference Proceedings, connected fabrication and post-treatment with film structure, transparency, and resistivity.
